correctness.rationale: Every strict increase is exactly membership in one of b-1 explicit affine intervals E_j; their images admit precisely nondecreasing branch itineraries. Each m-step branch cylinder has Lebesgue length ell_last/b^(m-1). The weighted hockey-stick identity gives binom(m+b-1,b-2)/((b-1)b^m). Full visitation has exact conditional probability binom(m-1,b-2)/binom(m+b-1,b-2). On full visitation the positive occupation compositions are equiprobable, converge to Dirichlet(1,...,1) spacings, and occur with probability tending to one. Geometric deviation from each branch's repelling fixed point sums to at most b on each surviving orbit, so W1(empirical, fixed-point mixture)<=b/m. The uniform-simplex and orbit-average laws follow, including the degenerate b=2 case. The finite independent rational checks (25 horizons, 456 cylinder masses) corroborate but are not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: The canonical rare event is a long strictly monotone ordinal word in an expanding Bernoulli map. Its probability has an exact base-dependent polynomial correction to exponential decay. More substantially, conditional orbit empirical measures converge to a Dirichlet-uniform random mixture of all repelling fixed-point measures, whereas unconditioned typical orbit empirical measures converge to Lebesgue; the selected orbital mean has an explicit nontrivial Irwin-Hall distribution for b>=3. This is a motivated, quantitative rare-event selection classification for an infinite natural family, not an arbitrary finite enumeration.
